name: 50 Hz head exposure, part 2 of 2 (Ghione 2005)
origin: Ghione, Del Seppia et al. (CNR Pisa), 2005
summary: Second half of the 90-min 50 Hz head exposure after Ghione et al. 2005: 45 more minutes of a 50 Hz sine on all eight ring coils in phase. Ghione's field was 40 or 80 uT peak, uniform over the head; this helmet gives 5 uT at 20 mm from each coil and about 0.3 to 0.5 uT at 60 mm, so only the frequency and timing are copied. Run it straight after part 1.
notes: Ghione et al. 2005 exposed 40 healthy men for 90 min to a 50 Hz field of 40 or 80 uT peak, 'as measured at the centre of the coils': two circular Helmholtz-like coils, 44 cm in diameter, 50 turns each, around the head with the head at the centre (p.2 [113]). The study was sham-controlled and double-blind. Each man had two 90-min sessions, field and sham, 1 to 2 weeks apart, and read a magazine during the exposure (p.2 [113]). The authors report that EEG alpha, measured afterwards, almost doubled at 80 uT and that the pain threshold fell at 40 uT. This program plays a 50 Hz sine on all eight ring coils in phase. Eight coils on the scalp do not make a field that is uniform over the head. The 90 min exceed the 60-min program limit and are split into two 45-min parts with short fades; start part 2 straight after part 1. Ghione's 40 or 80 uT peak was measured at the centre of the coil pair. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. The helmet gives 5 uT there (8.4 uT at its maximum), 8 to 16 times less, and about 0.3 to 0.5 uT at 60 mm. The finding comes from one lab. The alpha result rests on 15 of the 20 men of the 80 uT group; the recordings of 10 men (40 uT) and 5 men (80 uT) were discarded (p.2 [113]). Legros 2012 found no EEG effect after 1 h at 60 Hz and 1800 uT (balance and tremor changed), and mains pickup makes 50 Hz EEG studies prone to artefacts. Avoid if you have epilepsy (WHO notes greater susceptibility to induced fields, although the field here is tiny); stop on discomfort. The app's Blind option draws real or sham anew for each run, so it can mix them across the two parts; for a blinded 90-min copy, have a helper secretly choose the arm and run both parts, or the Sham (no field) program twice. If the coils hum audibly, mask the sound in both arms.
setting: Seated; Ghione's subjects read a magazine during the exposure (Ghione 2005 p.2 [113]). EEG alpha was measured after the exposure.
schedule: One 90-min exposure: part 1, then part 2 without a break. In the study each person had two 90-min sessions, field and sham, 1 to 2 weeks apart (Ghione 2005 p.2 [113]).
source: Ghione et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15911132/ ; Legros et al. 2012, Eur J Appl Physiol https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21894451/ ; WHO Environmental Health Criteria 238, Extremely low frequency fields (2007) https://inchem.org/documents/ehc/ehc/ehc238.pdf
